 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the claimant/injured challenging the judgment and award dated 4.5.2018 passed in MVC No.2560/2014 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT,
Bailhongal (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

I have heard the learned counsel Sri. Hanamant R Latur for the appellant/injured and learned counsel Sri. R.R. Mane for the respondent/Insurance Company.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he is restricting the present appeal only insofar as direction of the Tribunal to respondent No.1/owner of the vehicle to pay compensation, on the ground that the driver on wheel was not having Driving License to drive LGV (Transport) as on the date NC: 2024:KHC-D:6426 of the accident.
He submits that the said issue is no more res- integra in view decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal by directing the respondent/insurer to pay compensation to the appellant/injured.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent/Insurer supports the impugned judgment and award and seeks dismissal of the appeal.
He further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding rate of interest at 9% per annum and seeks to modify the same at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

7. The Tribunal has committed an error in directing the respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle to pay compensation on the ground that the driver of the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-24/7200 was not having valid and effective driving license to drive LGV(Transport).

2
Admittedly, AIR 2017 SC 3668 NC: 2024:KHC-D:6426 the driver on wheel was in possession of driving license to driver LMV(NT).
The said issue is no more res-integra in view of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan referred supra.
Admittedly, the vehicle in question was less than 7500 kgs.

Keeping in mind the enunciation of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment referred supra, this Court is of the considered view that the respondent/insurance company is liable to pay the compensation amount to the appellant/claimant with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
8. In modification of the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal to the aforesaid extent, the appeal stands allowed.

Sd/-
